lineas.texto: In the eighteen hundreds, men dug under rivers, and some came back up unable to walk.
To dig there, they needed the river kept out.
So the tunnel was filled with compressed air, pushing the water back.
But breathing air under pressure pushes extra nitrogen into your blood.
Come back up too fast, and that gas forms bubbles, like opening a soda.
Bubbles in the joints. Terrible pain. Workers called it the bends.
Even the Brooklyn Bridge's chief engineer got it, and ran the job from his window.
The fix was to come up slowly, so the gas can leave gently. Today, machines do most of the digging.
